narration.what: Clicked twice in the empty area of the Framer project dashboard's scroll area, below and to the left of the project thumbnails.
narration.why: To dismiss focus from the project grid and settle the pointer before choosing a project to open.

narration.what: Typed into the sidebar's Search field, entering "tr" then "een", deleting with backspace, retyping "ung", deleting again, and finishing with "fe", while the project grid reloaded as "Results".
narration.why: To filter the project list down to the one he wanted to open, correcting the query as he went.

narration.what: Opened the Treeunfe project and scrolled at length through its canvas, panning across the page frames while the Agent panel on the right showed the results of a "Find Unlinked Colors" run.
narration.why: To survey the project's layout and read through the list of unlinked colors the agent had reported.

narration.what: Scrolled the canvas onto a frame holding two video embeds and selected the "YouTube" layer inside Variant 1, opening its Style panel with the YouTube properties — Video URL, Autoplay, Mute, Color and Radius.
narration.why: To inspect how the existing YouTube embed component was configured on the page.

narration.what: With the Height field in the Style panel focused, nudged the value down with repeated Down-arrow presses, leaving the frame's height at 608, then clicked away into the document.
narration.why: To shrink the selected frame's height by small steps rather than typing a number, and then drop focus once the size looked right.

narration.app: Framer / Google Chrome / Captura de Tela / Dock
narration.what: Selected the YouTube layer in the Layers panel and worked through its component properties in the Style panel — the video link, Autoplay, Mute, Color and Radius fields — alongside Width and Height, then moved out to Chrome and the screenshot tool before clicking Figma in the Dock.
narration.why: To check how the embedded YouTube player was configured on the frame and then switch over to Figma to pull in the reference for the layout.

narration.what: Brought Figma up from the Dock — the frame catches the Dock with Figma's label showing over the Framer canvas — and clicked twice near the top-left of its window, then once just below in the scrollable panel there.
narration.why: To get into Figma and reach the file holding the design being rebuilt in Framer.

narration.what: In Figma's file browser search field, typed toward "tree" — backspacing through a first stab at "thre" and retyping the letters until it read "tree" — then pressed Down to highlight a suggestion and Enter to open it, landing on the Treeunfe file.
narration.why: To find and open the Figma file for the Treeunfe project, the design being rebuilt in Framer.

narration.what: Scrolled through the Cover page canvas in Figma, past the brand cover artwork down to the thumbnail frame, then clicked into a group on the canvas.
narration.why: To locate the frame they wanted before renaming it.

narration.what: Opened the Brand Guidelines page in Figma's Pages list and scrolled across its logo lockups, then switched to the Finder desktop and clicked a screenshot file named "Captura de Tela 2026-08-27 às 12.47.01".
narration.why: To compare the logo variants on the brand guidelines page against a screenshot saved earlier.

narration.what: Dragged the screenshot into the Figma canvas on the Brand Guidelines page, where it landed as an image layer named "Captura de Tela 2026-08-27 às 12.47.01" and came up selected with the image toolbar (Crop, Select area, Remove background, Edit with prompt), then switched to Chrome and typed "tiny" into a text field before returning.
narration.why: To bring the captured video still into the file as reference material and look up a tool for it in the browser.

narration.what: Brought up a Chrome window on tinypng.com beside the Figma file, scrolling its page past the "Drop your images here!" upload area and the product cards.
narration.why: To use TinyPNG to compress the screenshot before working with it further.

narration.what: Scrolled the page's scroll area and opened items with Enter, then clicked Framer in the Dock, entered Mission Control and picked the "Mesa 1" desktop, and clicked around inside the web area there.
narration.why: To bring Framer to the front on the desktop where that work was arranged, after finishing with the browser page.

narration.what: Scrolled at length through the site preview in Framer's Desktop breakpoint, reading down the page, then clicked the collapsed rows of the feature accordion to open and compare them.
narration.why: To review how the finished sections read and behave in the preview before making further edits.

narration.app: Figma / Framer / Google Chrome / Finder / Open and Save Panel Service (Framer)
narration.what: Saved a screenshot through the save panel with "Salvar", dragged that file — "Captura de Tela 2026-08-27 às 12.47.01 1.jpg" — from the desktop into the Figma canvas, then set its size to "1100" wide in the Dimensions fields and zeroed the position and corner radius values.
narration.why: To place the captured frame into the Figma file and size and align it precisely.

narration.what: Nudged the selected play-button frame rightward with repeated arrow-key presses, then one press up, and clicked in the Style panel around its Radius and BG Blur settings.
narration.why: To fine-tune the overlay button's position and appearance on the video variant.

narration.what: With the Star layer selected inside Variant 1, opened the Fill swatch in the Style panel and scrolled the color picker's style list under the "primary" group, clicking through its shade entries and settling on the "300" green.
narration.why: To recolour the selected shape using an existing project colour style rather than a one-off hex value, keeping it consistent with the palette already defined in the file.

narration.what: Switched the selection to the play-button Frame inside Variant 1 and paused over its Style panel — Interactions with a Click to Variant 2, Size, Fill, Radius, Border and BG Blur — while the colour picker sat open on the border colour with the "primary" style list scrolled into view.
narration.why: To take stock of how the play button is already built before changing its border colour.

narration.what: Scrolled the colour picker's style list further so the whole palette showed at once — the "base" group with white and black above the "primary" group's full ramp from 50 down through 800 — and hovered over one of the light shades near the top of the ramp.
narration.why: To see the full set of saved colour styles before picking which shade to give the play button's border.

narration.what: Kept scrolling the colour picker's style list past the end of the primary ramp into the "secondary" group, hovering over its early shades.
narration.why: To look beyond the primary palette for a border colour that suits the play button.

narration.what: Scrolled through the Color style picker popover open over the canvas, past the numbered swatch ramp down into the 'neutrals' group, and clicked in it.
narration.why: To find the swatch to apply as the fill for the selected play-button frame.

narration.what: Kept scrolling the Color popover into the 'neutral' group and clicked a swatch there, replacing the play button's green fill with a grey one on the canvas and in the Selection colors list.
narration.why: To try a neutral tone for the play button instead of the green it had.

narration.what: Clicked Align Middle and then Align Center in the Style panel to re-centre the play button on the frame, dismissed the Color popover, and switched the right sidebar to the Agent tab with the earlier 'Find Unlinked Colors' thread.
narration.why: To settle the button's position after the fill change and return to the agent conversation about unlinked colours.

narration.what: Back in the Style panel, typed "100" into the play button frame's Width and "100" into its Height, then clicked Align Center and Align Middle again to recentre it in the frame.
narration.why: To resize the play button to a square 100 by 100 and keep it centred on the video.

narration.what: With the play-button shape layer selected on the first video variant, nudged it with the right, left and up arrow keys and clicked around the canvas and the Shape section of the Style panel, where Position, Size, Points and Rotate are set.
narration.why: To bring the play icon into the middle of the video frame before switching to the Align Center and Align Middle buttons to place it exactly.

narration.what: Selected the Frame holding the play button in the Layers list and worked through its Style panel — nudging it with the arrow keys, setting Overflow to Clip from the dropdown, and opening the Fill colour picker, where the hex field and the project's saved colour styles are listed alongside Radius, Border and BG Blur.
narration.why: To turn the shape behind the play icon into a rounded, clipped, blurred button sitting over the video.

narration.what: Undid the last couple of style changes, set a field back to "0", reset the canvas zoom to 100%, then switched the right panel to the Agent tab and scrolled through the earlier "Find Unlinked Colors" conversation and its list of raw colours grouped by brancos, verdes, cinzas and azuis.
narration.why: To back out the button edits and re-read the agent's colour audit before deciding what to do about the unlinked colours.

narration.what: Selected the Frame layer for the play button in the Layers list and zoomed the canvas in on the first video variant with a "0" typed into the zoom control, panning the view while the Agent panel's colour audit stayed open on the right.
narration.why: To get a close look at how the play button now sits over the video before acting on the agent's colour findings.

narration.what: Scrolled back through the agent's "Find Unlinked Colors" reply in Framer's right-hand Agent panel, reading down the grouped lists of raw rgb values and the closing observations, then clicked out onto the canvas and the two video variant frames.
narration.why: To review the audit of colors not bound to the Color Guide before deciding how to respond to the agent's offer to create tokens.

narration.what: Opened the site in Framer's Preview at the Desktop 1200 breakpoint and scrolled the live page from the hero picker down past the customer logo band and the sections below, then clicked in the preview and up near the top-right controls.
narration.why: To see the page's real colors rendered in the browser rather than in the canvas, checking the audit's findings against how the design actually looks.

narration.what: Back on the canvas with the video Frame selected, clicked into the Height field in the Style panel's Size row and pressed the Down arrow three times to nudge the value down to 613.
narration.why: To fine-tune the height of the video frame inside the story section by small increments rather than typing a number.

narration.what: Kept pressing the Down arrow in the Height field, taking the video frame's height down again so its bottom edge pulled up inside the green story card.
narration.why: To keep shrinking the frame step by step until the padding below the video matched the space above it.

narration.what: Scrolled back up through the site preview in Framer's canvas, past the hero and the customer logo band, then clicked once in the preview area.
narration.why: To review how the page reads from the top after the latest changes before going back to typing.

narration.what: Widened the preview to a 2308-pixel desktop breakpoint and scrolled down through the dark integrations sections, clicking on the AI-assistant card group and its tab row along the way.
narration.why: To check how the API and AI integration sections hold up at a wider desktop width.

narration.what: Left the preview back to the canvas and selected the video Frame inside Variant 1 in the Layers panel, bringing up its Position & Size, Layout and Styles properties on the right.
narration.why: To inspect how the video component's two variants are set up before adjusting them.

narration.what: Selected the video Frame inside the green story section and, in the Style panel's Size fields, typed "11" over the Width value while its Radius stayed at 12.
narration.why: To resize the embedded video frame within the section it sits in.

narration.what: Scrolled and clicked around the Framer canvas showing the two YouTube video variants, with the Variant 2 YouTube layer selected and its Style panel open on the right.
narration.why: To inspect how the placed YouTube component renders in each variant before adjusting its settings.

narration.what: Typed "1161" into the Width field of the Size section in the Style panel for the selected video Frame, correcting the value with a delete along the way.
narration.why: To resize the embedded video frame to a specific pixel width so it fits the section layout.

narration.what: Finished the Width entry as "1161px", tabbed over to the Height field and set it to "558px", then opened the size dropdown and chose "Fill".
narration.why: To give the video frame the exact dimensions of the original and let it fill its container.

narration.what: Typed "92%" into the Width field, replacing the Fill setting so the video frame sits at a relative width inside its section.
narration.why: To inset the video slightly from the edges of the green section rather than spanning it edge to edge.

narration.what: Scrolled through the whole preview of the Treeunfe landing page in Framer, from the hero section down past the logo wall to the footer, clicking into the canvas a few times along the way.
narration.why: To review how the finished page reads end to end at desktop width before going back to adjust the canvas zoom.

narration.what: With the video Frame selected in the Layers panel, typed "905" into the Width field under Size in the right-hand properties panel and tabbed out of it.
narration.why: To set an exact width on the video block instead of dragging it, so it lines up with the section around it.

narration.what: Kept working the Size fields for the selected video Frame — re-entered "905px" for Width, tabbed across to set Height to "508px", picked "Fill" from the sizing dropdown, and typed "92%" — leaving the frame blown up to a height of 4996.
narration.why: To find a width and height combination that fits the video into the story section, though the Fill setting stretched it far past the intended size.

narration.what: Opened the live preview again and scrolled the page from the top through the logo wall and on down, clicking on the embedded YouTube video in the story section a few times along the way.
narration.why: To check in the running page whether the resized video block now sits correctly and still plays.

narration.what: Scrolled through the Framer canvas showing the two YouTube video variants, clicked into the embedded video area, then switched to Claude from the Dock and clicked around its scroll area before returning to Framer to look at the video frame again.
narration.why: To compare the video embed behaving on the canvas against the guidance in the Claude conversation, moving between the two windows to check what still needed changing.

narration.what: Typed a new prompt into Claude's message box — "quero criar um code component leve, performativco para framer onde eu colo um link do youtub" — backspacing mid-word while writing "performativo" and still typing when the moment ended.
narration.why: To ask Claude for a lightweight, performant Framer code component that takes a pasted YouTube link, instead of continuing to fight the video embed by hand on the canvas.

narration.what: Continued the prompt in Claude's message box with "e ele vira um player clean sem controles, quero que limpe a UI", backspacing over a stray "l" before "clean" and correcting "lime"/"ape" as he went.
narration.why: To spell out what the component should produce — a controls-free player with the YouTube chrome stripped out.

narration.what: Finished the prompt with "o maximo que conseguir sem gambiarras" — backspacing over the typo "conseugir" to fix it — and pressed Enter to send the whole request to Claude.
narration.why: To set the constraint that the UI be cleaned up as far as possible without hacks, and hand the request over for Claude to build.

narration.what: In the Claude chat "Player YouTube minimalista para Framer", he typed a follow-up into the message box — "qual o proximo paso? ja" — then stepped back through the text with the arrow keys to insert a missing letter before finishing " fiz todos os testes" and pressing Return; while the reply came in he clicked around the conversation's scroll area and the reply blocks, pointing at parts of the answer.
narration.why: To tell Claude the testing was already done and ask what the next step should be, then walk through the answer as it appeared.

narration.what: With the video frame selected on the Framer canvas, he typed into the Alt Text field of the image Fill popover — "Vídeo institucional Treeunfe" — then clicked back out onto the canvas.
narration.why: To give the frame's image fill a descriptive alt text naming the video and the brand before moving on.

narration.what: He scrolled down the Framer canvas through the page frames — past the video section and the "Números que falam por nós" stats — with the Agent panel's unlinked-colours report open on the right.
narration.why: To look over the rest of the page layout where the video sits before deciding what to change next.

narration.what: He kept scrolling the Framer canvas further down the desktop and mobile frames, past the stats row and testimonial block into the pricing section, then clicked on a group within one of the frames.
narration.why: To review the lower sections of the page and pick out the element he wanted to work on next.

narration.what: In the Claude desktop app, started a fresh conversation with the "Novo" button, then began a new prompt with "Esse plugin abaixo criado por você" before switching back to Framer's code view.
narration.why: To hand Claude the carousel plugin code in a clean chat instead of continuing the long thread already loaded with the Color Guide audit.

narration.what: Continued typing in Claude's new-chat message box, extending the prompt to "Esse plugin abaixo criado por você disponibiliza vídeos de um canal do youtube específico, porém ele ".
narration.why: To describe what the existing carousel plugin already does before stating the change he wants made to it.

narration.what: Kept typing the complaint — "funciona quando quer, mais ou menso " — then backspaced away a false start at the figure, first "50R" and then "40", settling on "os 40% das vezes ele buga e nao mostra".
narration.why: To pin down how often the carousel fails, since an intermittent bug needs a frequency to be diagnosable.

narration.what: Finished the symptom description — "fica todos em tela preta eu tenho que dar um refresh na página", fixing the typo "tendho" and the stray accent in "pa'" — then switched to the Chrome window holding the channel's YouTube page and clicked around its scroll area.
narration.why: To spell out the black-screen-until-reload failure for Claude, and to go back to the live page where the broken carousel can be seen.

narration.what: Continued typing the bug report in Claude's chat composer, extending it with ". quero que investigue e " after describing that the plugin's videos show a black screen until the page is refreshed.
narration.why: To ask Claude to investigate the cause of the plugin failure rather than just acknowledge the symptom.

narration.what: Finished the prompt in the Claude chat composer with "resolve esse erro de forma definitiva." and clicked in the message area.
narration.why: To close the request by demanding a permanent fix for the black-screen bug, not just a diagnosis.

narration.what: Inserted ", descubra" mid-sentence so the prompt read "quero que investigue, descubra e resolve esse erro de forma definitiva.", then left Claude to work in Chrome and Framer — opening the plugin's code, scrolling through it, and clicking Salvar.
narration.why: To sharpen the request into investigate-find-fix, and to pull up the plugin source the bug report refers to.

narration.what: Scrolled the Framer canvas through the site's sections and clicked into it, with the YouTubeCarousel layer selected and its component properties (Channel, Videos, Speed, Arrows) open in the right panel.
narration.why: To locate the YouTube carousel component on the page and inspect its settings before handing the bug over.

narration.what: Scrolled down the Framer canvas through the desktop and tablet breakpoint frames of the landing page, past the hero, the two emission-option cards and the customer logo band, then clicked on the canvas.
narration.why: To review how the page reads further down and to set focus back on the canvas before continuing to edit.

narration.what: Right-clicked the selected card group on the desktop frame, opening Framer's context menu with Add To Agent, Create Component, Fit Content, Replace With, Duplicate and Add Stack.
narration.why: To see which actions are available for the selected element before choosing one.

narration.what: Dismissed the context menu and panned the canvas sideways until the tablet and phone breakpoint frames of the page were in view alongside the desktop one.
narration.why: To compare how the same section lays out across the narrower breakpoints.

narration.what: Pointed at the two option cards on the desktop frame, opened a menu and picked Hover, then clicked a text field and pressed the arrow key to step through it.
narration.why: To inspect the cards' hover state and check the text inside them.

narration.what: In the Hover Effect popover, clicked into the second Offset field and nudged its value with the down and up arrow keys, settling on a small negative Y offset.
narration.why: To fine-tune how far the card lifts on hover by stepping the offset one unit at a time instead of typing a number.

narration.what: With the Hover Effect's Fill swatch open, scrolled through the color picker's saved styles list — the base and primary ramps — and clicked a swatch, turning the card's hover fill dark.
narration.why: To set the hover state's background from the project's existing color styles rather than entering a one-off hex value.

narration.what: Kept scrolling the Fill picker's color styles past the primary ramp into the neutral ramp, trying successive swatches and watching the card's hover fill change from the dark tone to a very pale tint.
narration.why: To compare candidate hover colors against the card in the canvas and settle on one subtle enough for a hover state.

narration.what: Back in the Hover Effect popover — its Fill now showing the neutral "25" style just picked — stepped the second Offset field again with the down and up arrow keys, then clicked out onto the canvas and back onto the card group.
narration.why: To re-tune how far the card shifts on hover now that the lighter fill was chosen, and to drop the picker so the card could be seen in place.

narration.what: Scrolled the Framer canvas preview of the site all the way down past the page body to the bottom banner and footer, clicking around in the page area as they went.
narration.why: To review how the lower sections of the page render before working on them.

narration.what: In the Hover Effect panel, set the Scale field to "1.05" and then entered "0" in the neighbouring field below it.
narration.why: To give the selected card a subtle grow-on-hover effect.

narration.what: Scrolled the Style sidebar down and clicked through the Hover Effect popover's Offset fields, landing in the vertical offset input.
narration.why: To reach the offset controls and neutralise the hover shift now that Scale is doing the work.

narration.what: Pressed the up arrow key three times in the Z Index field in the Style sidebar to step its value up.
narration.why: To nudge the layer's stacking order up rather than typing a number.

narration.what: Panned and scrolled around the Framer canvas, clicking repeatedly on the page frame and its layers — with a Stack selected in the Layers panel — then clicked into the Z Index field in the right-hand properties panel, whose value became editable.
narration.why: To pick out the specific stacked element on the page and get its stacking-order property ready to type a new value into.

narration.what: Worked back and forth over the two hero cards — selecting them on the canvas and in the Layers panel, toggling Visible from the layer context menu on several of them, typing "175" into a numeric property field, and finally opening the Transition popover on the hover Effect, where the Ease is set to Ease In Out and the Time field is now active.
narration.why: To isolate which layer is responsible for the card's hover animation and tune its easing and duration.

narration.what: In Framer's New Component dialog, typed the component name — starting "Cart", backspacing the stray "t" to "Card", typing an underscore then deleting it, and settling on "Card Emissor" before confirming with Enter; then clicked "Hover" in the menu on the new component.
narration.why: To turn the selected hero card into a reusable component with a descriptive name, and start work on its hover variant.

narration.what: Entered the new "Card Emissor" component's own canvas via the breadcrumb, then panned and scrolled between its two stacked variants — "Variant 1" and the newly added "Variant 1 - Hover" — clicking the hover variant so its properties filled the right-hand panel.
narration.why: To compare the base and hover variants side by side and confirm the hover state was created as a proper variant of the component.

narration.what: Scrolled through the colour picker's style list, past the entries under "base" and "primary", while the Fill colour popover stayed open over the Style panel of the selected hover variant.
narration.why: To look through the existing colour styles for the one to apply as the fill, rather than entering a hex value by hand.

narration.what: Worked through the Style panel on the hover variant of the card — picked colour styles from the Fill popover's list under "base" and "primary", set a Position dropdown to "Relative", and used the right-click menu to Copy an Effect and Paste it onto another layer, ending with a text field focused.
narration.why: To dress the hover state of the card with the project's shared colour styles and carry the same effect across to the matching layer instead of rebuilding it.

narration.what: Named a new component "Card Software" in the New Component dialog and confirmed it, then set Position Type to "Relative" twice in the Style panel and added a "Hover" state from the context menu on the new component.
narration.why: To turn the second card into its own reusable component with the same relative positioning and hover behaviour as the first one.

narration.what: Inside the new Card Software component, scrolled the colour picker down through the "primary" and "secondary" style groups while the hover variant was selected, then copied a property from the right-click menu.
narration.why: To reuse the same shared colour style and settings on the software card's hover state that were already applied to the first card.

narration.what: Scrolled through the colour list in the Fill popover on the selected card variant, moving past the "primary" swatch group down toward "secondary", then clicked into the list to pick a colour for the card's Border.
narration.why: To find the right shade in the project's saved colour styles rather than entering a colour value by hand.

narration.what: Kept scrolling the Fill popover past the earlier swatch groups into the "neutral" set and clicked the "100" swatch, which replaced the card's Fill of "white" and tinted the hover variant on the canvas.
narration.why: To fill the hover state of the card with a soft neutral from the project's saved styles instead of plain white.

narration.what: Scrolled the Fill popover back up through the swatch groups and clicked the neutral "50" swatch, changing the hover card's Fill from "100" to the lighter "50".
narration.why: To try a subtler tint for the hover state after the previous shade read too heavy against the primary card.

narration.what: Tried the green swatches in the Fill popover on the hover card, which turned it mint, then worked through the layers and canvas — pasting a copied element, setting a position to "Relative" from a context menu, and twice choosing "Reset Override" — while arrowing between variants.
narration.why: To test a green tint for the hover state and then undo the overrides that experiment left behind on the card's layers.

narration.what: Scrolled through the saved color styles list in the Fill popover, past the "base" group into "primary", and clicked on the swatch row for the "50" style.
narration.why: To pick an existing color style from the project palette for the selected element's fill rather than entering a new hex value.

narration.what: Kept scrolling the Fill popover's style list past the "primary" shades down to the "secondary" group, clicking one swatch after another and clicking back onto the two card variants on the canvas between tries.
narration.why: To try the palette's shades against the card and see which one reads right before settling on a fill.

narration.what: Left the canvas and opened Framer's preview of the card, moving the pointer over and away from the card and clicking it to run the hover variant.
narration.why: To watch the hover transition play in a live preview rather than judging it from the two static variants on the canvas.

narration.what: Clicked into the Chrome address bar on the tab showing the site's "Não é possível acessar esse site" DNS error page and pressed reload, while Framer's publish panel behind it still read "Updating…".
narration.why: To retry loading the published Framer site once the update finished, since the domain had not resolved yet.

narration.what: Switched to the browser window showing the published site at treeunfe.framer.website, which returned the DNS error page "Não é possível acessar esse site"; edited and re-entered the address, reloaded the page repeatedly with the reload shortcut, and dismissed the panel with the close button while Framer's publish sidebar still read "Updating...".
narration.why: To check whether the newly published Framer site was reachable yet, retrying the address until the publish finished propagating.

narration.what: Reloaded the failing page several times, then typed "framer" and "g1" into the browser address bar to load other sites, entered "2" in a field, picked "Reset Override" from a context menu, and opened Framer's Settings sidebar to Hosting → Domains, where the Base and Custom URLs both showed status READY.
narration.why: To work out whether the site itself was broken or the connection was — checking other sites still loaded, then confirming in the Domains settings that the custom domain was published and ready.

narration.what: Clicked an icon in the macOS menu bar, then returned to the Framer canvas and clicked into the desktop breakpoint's hero area, selecting the "Card Emis…" layer in the Layers panel, with the Agent panel still showing its "Find Unlinked Colors" results.
narration.why: To pick out the specific card on the canvas that the agent's unlinked-colour report pointed at, so its styling could be checked against the Color Guide.

narration.what: Opened the site in Framer's Desktop 1200 preview and worked through the page — clicking the hero cards and scrolling past the customer-logo band — typing "tre" into a field and taking a suggestion with the arrow key and Enter, entering "0.2", and twice picking "Reset Override" from the context menu.
narration.why: To try the page as a visitor would and clear stray overrides left on the elements being checked.

narration.what: Scrolled and clicked through the canvas and the Style panel of the "Card Emissor" component — selecting the card frames and their nested Stack layers, tapping the space bar to pan, and settling on the layer whose Layout, Styles, Transition and Opacity settings fill the right-hand inspector.
narration.why: To inspect how the card variant and its hover state are configured before adjusting the transition and opacity values.

narration.what: In the Clients section of the canvas, selected a client logo's vector layer and renamed it "Exit Lag" in the Layers list, then clicked back onto the artwork on the canvas.
narration.why: To give the logo layer the client's own name so the list of client logos is identifiable.

narration.what: Corrected the name still being edited on the canvas — deleting characters and retyping an "l" so the layer reads "Exit Lag" rather than the misspelling — then clicked on empty canvas to commit it.
narration.why: To fix the spelling of the client logo layer's name before moving on.

narration.what: Zoomed back out to the full page layout and clicked the client-logo cell in the green logo grid, bringing up its Clients properties in the Style panel with the icon set to "Exitlag".
narration.why: To check that the renamed logo is the one wired into that slot of the client grid.

narration.what: Scrolled at length through the Framer canvas across the site's sections — the pricing/plan cards, the "Quem emite com a Treeunfe" logo wall, and the fiscal-notes section — clicking into the canvas and layer groups along the way, removing an item from a context menu, then opening the CleanMyMac menu bar item and pressing "Liberar" under "Memória" before clicking the Visual Studio Code and Calendário icons in the Dock.
narration.why: To review the layout of the design in the canvas, then free up memory and switch to other apps.

narration.what: Selected the Phone breakpoint's Grid layer holding the two cards and stepped its Gap field in the Style panel with the arrow key, keeping Height at Fill and Max Width at 480 Fixed.
narration.why: To tighten the spacing between the two cards so they fit side by side on the phone layout.

narration.what: With the Frame layer selected on the phone breakpoint, he clicked into the Height field in the Size section of the Style panel and pressed the up arrow key several times to raise the value, clicking back onto the canvas and the layer between adjustments, and pressed "k".
narration.why: To fine-tune the height of the selected frame by nudging it up step by step and checking the result on the canvas after each change.

narration.what: In the Scale tool panel he nudged the icon's size with the arrow keys, then deleted and undid the change, worked down the layer list selecting the nested Solid, Path and Button layers, switched a variant dropdown from "Variant 1" to "Variant 2" and back again, and chose "Reset Override" from the context menu on the phone frame's element.
narration.why: To get the icon inside the phone breakpoint back to its intended size and variant after the scaling attempt, by undoing the change and clearing the override it left behind.

narration.what: With the SVG "Solid" layer selected inside the phone frame, he nudged it around the canvas with the left and arrow keys, then opened the Size dropdown in the Style panel, picked "Fit Content", and immediately switched it back to "Fixed".
narration.why: To reposition the small graphic in the phone breakpoint and test whether letting it size to its content behaved better than a fixed size, reverting when it did not.

narration.what: He entered Framer's preview at the Phone breakpoint and scrolled the page all the way down to the footer, clicking on the contact tiles and links there, then hit the "Update" button before heading back.
narration.why: To see the edited section behave in a real phone-width preview and check the footer area's links and cards, refreshing the preview to pick up the latest canvas changes.

narration.what: Clicked through the Tablet and Phone breakpoint previews of the Treeunfe page in the Framer canvas, scrolling down both and picking "Variant 2" from a component's variant menu, while the agent panel's "Find Unlinked Colors" report stayed open on the right.
narration.why: To check the regenerated responsive layouts against the agent's colour audit before accepting the update.

narration.what: Opened the "animation-copia-right" component for editing, selected a nested layer inside Variant 1's ticker stack and set its Width and Height fields in the Style panel's Size section, tabbing between the two and confirming each with Enter.
narration.why: To resize the icon tile inside the animated component so it matches across the two variants.

narration.what: Selected a nested layer inside Variant 2's ticker stack on the canvas and set its sizing to "Fit Content" from the size dropdown, then switched the right panel back from Style to the Agent tab showing the colour report.
narration.why: To let the layer size itself to its contents instead of a fixed value, matching the other variant.

narration.what: Selected the Variant 2 frame in the Layers list and canvas, then stepped its Width field in the Style panel's Position & Size section up and down with the arrow keys while watching the variant redraw.
narration.why: To dial in the variant's frame width by eye so its two icon columns sit correctly.

narration.what: With a Stack layer selected, he put the cursor in the Height field under Position & Size in the right-hand Style panel and pressed the Down arrow key repeatedly to step the fixed height down, then clicked back onto the canvas and picked out layers in the Layers panel.
narration.why: To nudge the selected stack's height smaller in small increments and watch the effect on the artboard rather than typing an exact number.

narration.what: With both Ticker layers selected in the Layers panel, he clicked into the Gap field under Layout in the Style panel and nudged the value with the Down and Up arrow keys, stepping it down and then partway back up.
narration.why: To tighten the spacing between the ticker's items and find a gap that looked right on the canvas without committing to a typed number.

narration.what: He nudged the focused numeric field with the Down and Up arrow keys, then clicked into a size field in the Style panel and typed "8" followed by Return, before clicking around the ticker frames on the canvas and scrolling the properties panel down.
narration.why: To set an exact spacing value instead of continuing to step it, and then to reselect the ticker frames and check the rest of their properties.

narration.what: He worked over the Variant 2 tickers — selecting Ticker rows in the Layers panel, pressing Delete twice to remove items from them, stepping the Height field up with the Up arrow so it read as Fixed rather than Fit, and clicking through frames on the canvas and the breadcrumb trail above it.
narration.why: To prune the duplicated ticker contents and pin the row to a set height so the two ticker rows in Variant 2 line up the way he wanted.

narration.what: Nudged the selected Ticker layer with the arrow keys and clicked on the Variant 2 frame and the canvas, while the Height field in the Style panel sat focused for editing.
narration.why: To adjust the position and size of the ticker inside the second variant.

narration.what: Set the Ticker layer's Height to 50 and stepped the Gap field down with the arrow keys in the Style panel, clicking around the Variant 2 frame on canvas between adjustments, and typed "Sim pode seguir" into a chat elsewhere.
narration.why: To tighten the ticker's row height and spacing while approving the assistant to continue its work.

narration.what: Zoomed and panned the canvas back out to the Home page's tablet and phone breakpoints, chose "Clip" from a dropdown in the panel, and clicked into the card layers on canvas.
narration.why: To check how the edited card section looks across breakpoints and keep its contents clipped to the frame.

narration.what: Panned across to the desktop breakpoint and clicked the hero Section, which opened its Stack layout settings in the Style panel.
narration.why: To compare the two card blocks side by side on desktop and tablet and inspect the section's layout.

narration.what: Scrolled the Framer canvas across the Desktop and Tablet breakpoints, clicked into nested groups on the page and selected the matching Section layer in the Layers panel, then opened the Overflow control in the right-hand Style panel and picked "Clip" from its menu.
narration.why: To inspect how the hero and card section was built across breakpoints and stop its contents from spilling outside the frame by switching that section's overflow from visible to clipped.

narration.what: Opened the Framer preview at the Tablet breakpoint (806 × 1512) and scrolled steadily down the page, past the hero and the customer logo band into the sections below.
narration.why: To see how the section behaves at tablet width in a real preview after changing its overflow to Clip.

narration.what: Back on the canvas, selected the card group on the Tablet frame and worked through the Style panel — Overflow now reads "Clip", Direction and Distribute set to Start — then used the right-click menu's "Create Variable", pressed the "Update" button, and switched the component to "Variant 2" from its variant dropdown.
narration.why: To push the clipping fix into the shared component and check the alternate variant picks up the same layout at tablet width.
